subtitle: Lesson 31 · An illustrative, fictional case study

steps.label: Network segmentation, reviewed
steps.sub: No direct spoke-to-spoke peering between claims, quoting, integrations

steps.label: Cost and policy compliance, 100%
steps.sub: Firewall sized for +40% headroom; every subscription passed tagging rules

code:
Regional outage, primary region, ~6 hours.

Claims DB  -> failed over on schedule   (2hr RTO met)
Quoting DB -> failed over on schedule   (4hr RTO met)

Hub (firewall, gateway, DNS resolver)
  -> existed ONLY in the primary region
  -> never deployed to the secondary region

Result: every spoke's 0.0.0.0/0 route pointed at nothing.
caption: The applications failed over correctly. The network they failed over into didn't exist.

code:
1. The checklist was application-shaped
   -> "RTO/RPO per workload" produces a list of apps,
      not a shared network layer nobody owns

2. Ownership was ambiguous
   -> Platform built the hub; app teams wrote DR plans
      for their own workload only

3. The diagram implied symmetry
   -> Secondary region drawn next to primary looked
      complete -- only the app boxes were ever deployed there
caption: Three individually reasonable gaps combined into one blind spot.

eyebrow: The question that would have caught it

steps.label: "If the hub goes down, what happens to every spoke that depends on it?"
steps.sub: Forces shared services onto the same RTO/RPO checklist as every application

steps.label: This is exactly what ADR-003 does
steps.sub: Treats the hub as a DR-in-scope tier with its own explicit, tested target
